title: Kenya Red Cross: over 2 million people in 46 counties could be affected by El Niño rains
detail: Garissa and Tana River named at risk. Governor Nathif Jama convened a flood-preparedness meeting on the Tana; awareness campaign to move residents away from the riverline. Red Cross readiness 70–75%, 50+ boats ready.

title: Water CS warns Garissa and Tana River residents to prepare to move to higher ground
detail: Masinga, Kamburu, Gitaru, Kindaruma and Kiambere expected to spill if rainfall reaches projected levels; Bura canal can divert ~11,000 L/s if levels become critical.

title: CSG El Niño Watch issued
detail: Forecast rain on Mt Kenya first, the Tana rising later, flash floods in Garissa laghas as the first danger, and a Tana flood season at Garissa from early November if heavy rain persists.

title: Kenya Met: above-average rain expected for November–December
detail: Acting director Edward Muriuki warned of flooding, damaged roads and malaria, cholera and typhoid risk. Rain forecast for 46 counties incl. Garissa, 3–10 Nov.

title: Kenya Met weekly forecast 10–16 Nov: rain in parts of all 47 counties
detail: Garissa: sunny mornings, afternoon showers, maximum above 35 °C. Night showers in Tana River, Wajir, Mandera and the Mt Kenya counties.

title: Kenya Met 24-hour advisory: localised falls above 50 mm, flood risk
detail: Heavier rain over the Lake Basin, western, Rift Valley, central (incl. Nairobi) and northern parts, 12–13 Nov; isolated thunderstorms.

title: Heavy rain on Thursday night floods parts of Garissa
detail: Storm overnight 12–13 Nov flooded parts of Garissa. Open-Meteo analysis: ~30 mm at Garissa and Dadaab and 23 mm at Bura on 13 Nov; about 60 mm at Garissa over 9–15 Nov.

title: NDOC: 1.5 million people at risk; residents of flood-prone areas urged to move to higher ground
detail: Kenya Met expects November to be the peak of an above-normal October–December season.

title: FEWS NET: erratic, delayed start of the short rains; rain from the second week of November
detail: Drier and hotter than average September–October across much of Kenya; localised flooding in Tana River county in late October; intense November rain raises flood and waterlogging risk.

title: GloFAS: River Tana flow at Garissa ~3× early October and still rising
detail: Median forecast peaks around 28 Nov; wettest ensemble members more than double that. CSG starts daily River Tana monitoring.
